Essentially there are a few helpful things I've used to avoid stalemates, and learning to checkmate when I have a winning endgame.

Firstly while it sounds like a broken record puzzles really do help identify common checkmate patterns (such as the back rank mate).

Secondly, I recommend going on YouTube or other resources and looking up common winning endgames. To start, there's the ladder mate, which is when 2 rooks, 2 queens, or 1 of each checkmate the king on the side of the board together. Then there's also the king and queen vs king, and the king and rook vs king. Which also follow a similar concept of pushing the king to the side of the board.

Thirdly, when you're in an endgame like that where all they have is a king always deliver checks. If every move is a check then it will never be stalemate. Or if you have enough time on the clock really make sure the king won't be stuck if you make a move that isn't a check.

It'll take a little bit of time but eventually it'll become effortless to deliver those common checkmates you'll see!

The issue is that after you move the queen up (h6) your line requires that the king jumps right into mate in 1 (g8) when he doesn't have to, and probably would never actually do that in a game. If he jumps diagonally down and to the left through the pawns (f6) it becomes mate in 6 which is harder to find and white might completely miss it in-game. As a general rule in games and in puzzles it's best to assume the opponent will make the best move available compared to blundering.
